title: Define crystal‑field Hamiltonian and compute matrix elements
action: Set up the one‑electron crystal‑field Hamiltonian for C₂ symmetry, numerically compute matrix elements of the tesseral spherical tensor operators C_q^k, and fix the coordinate rotation such that S_2^2 = 0.
description: This step builds the theoretical model needed for the fitting procedure. No output file is written; the implementation is used internally by subsequent steps.

title: Fit crystal‑field parameters with Nelder‑Mead optimization
action: Using the provided 22 observed Stark energies and the initial guess from Er³⁺ in Y₂O₃, perform a nonlinear least‑squares fit via the Nelder‑Mead algorithm to minimize the root‑mean‑square deviation between calculated and observed energies. Save the final fitted parameters and the achieved rms deviation.
description: Contains the 14 fitted crystal‑field parameters (B_q^k, S_q^k) and the rms deviation (σ) between the calculated and observed Stark energies.
output_schema: JSON object with keys: B0_2, B2_2, B0_4, B2_4, B4_4, S2_4, S4_4, B0_6, B2_6, B4_6, B6_6, S2_6, S4_6, S6_6 (real numbers, unit cm⁻¹), and rms_deviation (float, cm⁻¹).

title: Compute calculated Stark energy levels
action: Using the fitted Hamiltonian parameters from step 2, compute the Stark energy levels for the ⁴I_15/2, ⁴I_13/2, ⁴I_9/2, and ⁴S_3/2 multiplets. Save the list of calculated levels in a CSV file.
description: The calculated Stark energies allow the verifier to recompute the rms deviation against the hidden observed energies.
output_schema: CSV table with columns: multiplet (string, e.g., '4I15/2'), level_index (integer starting at 1), calculated_energy_cm1 (float, unit cm⁻¹).

title: Calculate crystal‑field strength parameters
action: From the fitted crystal‑field parameters, compute the reduced strength parameters S_cf^k (k = 2, 4, 6) and the overall strength N_V using the published formulas. Save the values in a JSON file.
description: These derived parameters characterise the crystal‑field interaction and are used to compare with literature values.
output_schema: JSON object with keys: Scf2, Scf4, Scf6, NV (all floats, unit cm⁻¹).
